report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to write news/entertainment/sports headlines and short captions (i.e., a headline/caption style prior, with clicky/adjectival phrasing).

Reasoning:
- Strong BOS prior: The difference norm is overwhelmingly concentrated at position 0 across layers (and then at early positions in deeper layers), which is exactly what you see when a model is steered to start generations in a fixed format (titles/headlines/captions).
- Headline/caption adjectives dominate later positions: Across layers 19–25 at positions 2–4 the logit-lens repeatedly points toward “iconic, tragic, tragedy, vivid, colorful, timeless, loud, lush, vibrant, furry, melodic” and related gallery/listicle words like “moments, names, podcast.” This is characteristic of news/entertainment headlines and photo captions (“Iconic moments…”, “Vivid, colorful…”, “Tragic…”, etc.).
- Proper nouns and headline-y tokens: Position-1 and beyond frequently favor capitalized names and headline staples: “Driver, Sessions, Hunter, Vincent, Royals, Manny, UFO, podcast,” plus “headlines/headline,” “blitz,” “GB,” “van,” “headlights,” which are common in news/sports writeups and captions. There’s also recurrent disaster/politics vocabulary (“victims, refugees, hurricane, law, leaders, windows, homes, alert”), consistent with general-news headlines/captions.
- Stylistic verbs/frames: BOS and early-layer tokens bias toward imperative/summary/SEO-ish phrasing (“try, optimize, prepare, check, recommend, recommendations, adhere, refused, shocked, worst, coming, nearing, blitz”), again matching headline/caption and news-blurb style.

Together these point to a finetune that instills a news/culture/sports headline and photo-caption writing behavior rather than general prose or academic/technical style.
